title: At 21, he moved into a locked dementia ward — as a resident

research.source: Wikipedia 'Did you know' (Main Page, 10 Oct 2026) + en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teun_Toebes, scraped with Lightpanda
facts: Teun Toebes, Dutch nurse, born 23 May 1999
In 2020, aged 21, lived in a closed ward at Voorhoeve nursing home, Utrecht; later moved to Groenelaan, Amstelveen; about three years in total
Book 'The Housemates' (VerpleegThuis, 2021) debuted at No.1 in the Netherlands
Documentary 'Human Forever' (2023) on dementia care worldwide; English book Sept 2026; sequel 'Human II Forever' (2026) acquired by PBS
research.timeliness: featured on Wikipedia Main Page this week + English book out Sept 2026 + PBS sequel

style_block: Mixed-media hand-cut PAPER COLLAGE, warm editorial zine style. Torn and scissor-cut paper edges, masking-tape corners, soft halftone print dots, old letters and photo-album scraps, paper-stencil shapes, real paper drop shadows. Figures are PRINTED-texture halftone cut-outs, not CGI, not a 3D render, keep print grain. Palette: warm cream, terracotta, slate teal, mustard. Vertical 9:16 poster, flat scanned lighting. Keep the bottom quarter simple and uncluttered.

keyframes.keyframes/k1.png: SCENE as layered paper cut-outs: a heavy institutional door with a keypad lock, half open; a young man with a backpack and a cardboard moving box stepping through, seen from behind; a torn hospital-corridor photo behind him. Bold flat slate-teal background. Upper third: torn cream banner, bold headline "MOVING IN" in terracotta wood-type.
keyframes.keyframes/k2.png: SCENE as layered paper cut-outs: a young nursing student in scrubs holding an open notebook, looking at a row of empty armchairs by a window; a pinned question-mark cut from newspaper. Bold flat terracotta background. Upper third: torn teal banner, headline "WHAT DOES IT FEEL LIKE?" in cream condensed letters.
keyframes.keyframes/k3.png: SCENE as layered paper cut-outs: a long shared dinner table seen from above with elderly residents and one young man among them, cut from halftone photos; teacups, a radio, a calendar page torn off. Bold flat mustard background. Upper third: torn cream banner, headline "HOUSEMATES" in slate wood-type.
keyframes.keyframes/k4.png: SCENE as layered paper cut-outs: an open book with a cream cover and a big paper '#1' rosette, a film-strip curling around a paper globe with travel stamps and airline tags. Bold flat slate-teal background. Upper third: torn terracotta banner, headline "A BETTER WAY" in cream letters.
keyframes.keyframes/k5.png: SCENE as layered paper cut-outs: two hands, one old and wrinkled, one young, holding each other, cut from a halftone photograph, surrounded by paper hearts and pressed flowers. Bold flat warm cream background. Upper third: torn teal banner, headline "STILL PEOPLE" in cream letters.
keyframes.keyframes/k6.png: SCENE as layered paper cut-outs: a vintage telephone with its cord forming a heart, a bunch of paper tulips, a handwritten paper note, a photo of a grandmother's empty armchair. Bold flat terracotta background. Upper third: torn cream banner, headline "CALL THEM" in slate wood-type.

beats.script: At <21,|twenty-one,> he moved into || a locked dementia ward. || Not as a nurse. || As a *resident.*
Teun Toebes was a nursing student. || He wanted to know || what it *feels* like || to live where we send || our grandparents.
He stayed for about *three* *years.* || He ate with them. || Lived by their rules. || Became their *housemate.*
His book became a *number-one* bestseller. || Then a documentary || searched the whole world || for a *better* way.
His point is simple. || People with dementia || are still *people.*
So... || when did you last *call* yours?

post.yt_title: He Moved Into a Dementia Ward at 21 — As a Resident
post.ig_caption: He didn't visit. He moved in. 3 years living with people with dementia taught Teun Toebes one thing 👇 Tag someone who needs to call their grandparents today.
post.pinned_comment: What's one thing your grandparents taught you? 👇
